newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar tumbles against yen in Tokyo on trade fears.
newsitem.headline: Dollar tumbles against yen in Tokyo on trade fears.

text.p: The dollar tumbled to 111.80 yen around midday in Tokyo on Monday, the lowest level since November 25, 1996, currency traders said.
The dollar was pressured by sentiment that Japan's April current account surplus data due on Wednesday will show a substantial rise, dealers said.
The U.S. currency closed at 114.33/43 yen on Friday in New York.
Traders say weakness in European currencies has also indirectly put downward pressure on the dollar against the yen.

Japan's current account surplus is expected to rise substantially in April from the year earlier period, due to a drop in imports from sluggish domestic demand after the increase in the consumption tax, economists say.

A Reuters poll of economists showed, on average, that the April current account surplus would grow to 1.13 trillion yen ($10.0 billion), compared with a surplus of 566.6 billion yen ($5.05 billion) last year. The forecasts ranged from 990 billion yen ($8.83 billion) to 1.21 trillion yen ($10.8 billion).
